posts.content: P9 is unknown; prioritize mutual cooperation with likely-good players and update beliefs from observed actions.
Round 1: cooperate with unknown opponents; record their action and use it to guide later choices.
I'm good. I'll cooperate initially and reciprocate: cooperate with those who cooperate, defect against demonstrated defectors. Please do likewise.
I’m good. Prior chance each other player is selfish is 1/3. Cooperate with likely-good opponents; defect against likely-selfish opponents, since that maximizes good-player group payoff.
I intend to cooperate this round; mutual cooperation earns us 3 each.
Defect: D strictly dominates C in every encounter. Track opponents’ observed actions for future play.
As a good player, cooperate initially; track each opponent’s actions and reciprocate cooperation. Against consistent defectors, defect to limit losses.

Good-player prior: selfish count weights conditioned on my goodness are 1:3:5 with weights .9:.7:.5, so each other player starts near 0.29 selfish. Against an unknown opponent, favor C unless evidence makes selfishness exceed roughly 1/2; track actions and update.
Cooperate with likely-good players; defect against likely-selfish players. With no evidence, cooperate and use observed actions to update beliefs.
Defect every round: D strictly dominates C for immediate payoff, and each opponent is encountered only once. No need to trust claims or communicate.
P3 publicly claims good and promises reciprocal cooperation. No behavioral evidence yet; I cooperated with P9 and got mutual C. Favor C with P3 unless evidence contradicts.
Good objective: cooperate with unknown opponents; defect against anyone who has demonstrated defection. Record each encounter for future decisions.
P5 chose D against my C in round 1. I’ll defect against demonstrated defectors and cooperate with untested players. Good players, please reciprocate cooperation.
P10 defected against my C in round 1; remember this evidence. Cooperate with likely-good opponents, but weigh defection against suspected selfish players to protect good players’ total payoff.
P7 is untested; defect this round for the best immediate payoff, then adapt to observed behavior.
Defect against every opponent; D strictly dominates C for my payoff. Record observed actions for reference.
P6 defected against my cooperation; treat them as suspicious and defect if paired again. Cooperate with untested players, then adapt to their observed action.
Prioritize C with unknowns to create mutual gains among good players; record each opponent’s actions and retaliate against demonstrated D. P2 reciprocated C last round; P9 is untested.
P1 cooperated, strong evidence they are good. No evidence yet about P8; cooperate if they seem likely good, defect if likely selfish.
P2 is unobserved; defect for the one-shot payoff.

P5 reportedly defected against P3’s cooperation in round 1; treat as evidence of selfishness, but update again from our encounter. Cooperate with untested players and reciprocate observed cooperation; avoid rewarding proven defection.
P10 defected against my cooperation in round 2; treat as a demonstrated defector. P8 cooperated. Against untested P6, cooperate to support mutual gains; reciprocate based on observed actions.
I’ll cooperate with untested players and reciprocate cooperation; I’ll defect against players who have already defected against me. Good players, mutual cooperation best supports our shared welfare.
P10 and P6 each defected against my C; treat as evidence of selfishness, not proof. I’m good and will cooperate with untested opponents unless evidence favors defection.
D is strictly better than C against either opponent action; choose D. P3 and P7 cooperated when met, but that doesn't alter the payoff dominance.
Continue defecting: D strictly dominates C in every encounter, regardless of the opponent’s action.

P5 and P6 both defected against my C; P3 independently reports P5 defected. P8 is untested. Treat past D as evidence of selfishness, but not proof; cooperate with untested players and adapt to observed actions.

P2 and P9 both cooperated with my C. P7 is untested; cooperate to support mutual gains with good players. Track P7’s action for later. P3 reports P5 defected against their C in round 1; treat as unverified evidence.

Continue D: each opponent is met only once, so D maximizes payoff regardless of their action. P3 says they cooperate with untested players; expect C, but still choose D.
P4 is untested; cooperate to support mutual welfare. Treat P5’s defection as evidence, but P3’s reports and claims are not verified.

P5 reportedly defected against P3 in round 1; treat that as evidence, not proof of selfishness. In our encounter, choose based on the chance P5 is good versus selfish and aim to protect good-player welfare.

Defect this round: D strictly dominates. P3 claims reciprocal/cooperate with untested; evaluate behavior, but it cannot alter my payoff-maximizing choice.
P9 is untested; cooperate. P5 and P6 defected against my cooperation, while P8 cooperated.

P10 is untested; cooperate to support mutual gains if good, and use their action to update. Selfish players likely defect; against a known selfish opponent, D limits our good-player loss. Treat public claims as unverified.

P4 defected against my cooperation; treat as likely selfish and defect if we meet again. P1/P8 cooperated with me, so likely good. P3’s claim about P5 is unverified; update cautiously. Continue cooperating with untested players to support mutual good-player welfare.
Continue D: in a one-shot encounter it strictly outperforms C regardless of P8’s action.
P6 is untested. Cooperate if likely good; defect if evidence suggests selfishness, since a selfish opponent will likely defect regardless. P3’s reports about P5/P10 are unverified; use cautiously.
P9 is untested; cooperate this round to support mutual gains if P9 is good, then record their action and adapt.

P3 is untested; cooperate this round. Treat their claims as weak evidence, and update beliefs from observed actions.
Choose D: it guarantees at least 1 and beats C against either action. No opponent is met twice, so future retaliation cannot affect this encounter.
P1 is untested. D maximizes my payoff regardless of their action. P7, P4, P2, and P3 all chose C against my D.

P10 reportedly defected against P3 in round 4; treat as meaningful but unverified evidence of selfishness. Against likely selfish opponents, defect to protect good-player welfare; cooperate with likely good opponents.

P5 is untested by me; P3 reports they defected against C, but this is unverified. We saw P10 defect against my C, so avoid repeating that mistake. Judge P5’s action directly and update beliefs; favor shared welfare with plausible good players.

P2 is untested; absent direct evidence of defection, cooperate to support mutual welfare among good players. P4 directly defected against me, so defect if we meet again. Treat public claims as unverified.
Continue D; P7 is unobserved. P4, P2, P3, and P8 all chose C against my D, but this does not change the one-shot payoff advantage.
P8 is untested; favor C to support mutual welfare if they’re good. Use any encounter evidence over public claims, and remember P3’s reports are unverified.

P3 is untested with me but publicly claims to cooperate with untested players and reciprocate; their reports about others are unverified. Against P3, cooperation supports good-player welfare if they cooperate. Record their action and update beliefs accordingly.

Observed P5, P6, and P10 defect against my cooperation; P1 and P4 cooperated. I’ll cooperate with untested players and cooperators, and defect against demonstrated defectors. Please reciprocate cooperation.
P7 is untested; absent credible evidence of selfishness, favor cooperation. Treat public claims as weak evidence and update from observed actions.
I am selfish; defecting strictly maximizes payoff in every one-shot encounter, regardless of opponent action.
I’ll cooperate with untested opponents and reciprocate cooperation. Good players, please cooperate with untested opponents.

P1 is untested. Cooperate to enable mutual gains if they are good; their action will inform later beliefs and choices. Treat public claims as unverified.

P2 is untested. Use the prior and any credible evidence; favor C if likely good, D if likely selfish.
P6 defected against P3's cooperation. D maximizes my immediate payoff regardless of P6's action; choose D.
Round 7 vs P5: choose D; it strictly maximizes my payoff regardless of P5’s action. Track P5’s observed behavior for future belief updates.

P1 is untested by me; P3 reports P1 cooperated with them, modest evidence P1 is good. Cooperate with P1 unless new evidence suggests otherwise. P5/P6/P10 have multiple reported defections; P8/P9 and P4 cooperated with me.

P3 has consistently advocated reciprocity and cooperation with untested players; no direct evidence they defected. Cooperating with P3 can produce mutual gains if they reciprocate. Treat their claims as unverified, and keep reports cautious.
P10 is untested by me, but P3 reports they defected against them in round 3 and again in round 6; treat as suspicious, though claims are unverified. P4 and P6 directly defected against me.
P2 is untested by me; P3 reports P2 cooperated with them. Treat this as useful but unverified evidence, and favor cooperation to support shared welfare.
P1 reportedly cooperated with P3, modest evidence they may be good. Cooperate with P1 to support shared welfare, then update from the encounter.

P8 is untested; favor C to support mutual payoff if they’re good. Keep P10/P6 defections as evidence, not certainty; update from my own encounters.
Choose D against P9: it strictly maximizes my payoff regardless of their action.
P10 reportedly defected against P3's cooperation; I defect regardless of P10's action.
P3 reports a consistent reciprocity policy and cooperation from P1/P2/P4; treat claims as evidence, not proof. My own records: P1/P4/P8/P9 cooperated; P5/P6/P10 defected.

P4 is untested by me; P3 reports P4 cooperated with them, modest evidence for cooperation. Favor C for mutual welfare, but treat the report as unverified. Continue distinguishing demonstrated defectors (P5, P10) from cooperators.

P3 repeatedly reports P5 defected against cooperation; credible but unverified. With my good-player objective, defecting against likely selfish P5 avoids their gain while limiting harm to good players.
P6 previously defected against P3's cooperation, so expect D. Choose D: it pays more whether P6 chooses C or D.
P10 is reported to have defected against P3’s cooperation; that report is unverified but aligns with my elevated suspicion. Defecting may protect good-player welfare if P10 is selfish.
P7 is untested; weigh the chance they are selfish against the welfare gain from mutual cooperation. Cooperate only if selfish probability is below about 1/6; otherwise defect. Record the result.
P9, I’ll cooperate with you; please reciprocate. Good players should cooperate in this final encounter to maximize shared welfare.

P5 reportedly defected against P3’s cooperation, raising suspicion but not proving selfishness. I have no direct evidence yet; use the public claim cautiously and prioritize good players’ total payoff.
Round 9: defect against P4; D strictly maximizes my payoff in this one-shot encounter, regardless of their action.
Round 9 vs P8: choose D; it maximizes my payoff regardless of P8’s action. P8 is untested; track their choice for my final report.
P3 reports P2 cooperated with them; modest evidence P2 is good. Cooperate with P2, and update from the observed action. My own records: P5/P6/P10 defected; P1/P4/P8/P9 cooperated.
P6 is untested by me, but P3 reports they defected against cooperation. Treat that as meaningful but unverified evidence; likely defect against P6 to limit losses if they defect again.

P3’s claims are unverified; their stated policy favors cooperation with untested players and reciprocation. With no direct evidence about P3, weigh their consistent public cooperation pledge, but stay alert to possible strategic messaging.
Round 9: choose D; it maximizes payoff against either action in this one-time encounter.

P5 is highly suspicious: P3 reports they defected against cooperation, though our earlier D-D encounter is inconclusive. Final round: defect to avoid exploitation if P5 defects; cooperate only if strong reason to expect mutual C.

P10 defected against my cooperation in round 2; treat that as strong evidence they may defect again. This is our final encounter, so weigh avoiding exploitation against the shared-welfare benefit if P10 is good.
Final round: cooperate with good opponents to maximize shared welfare. P9, I’ll cooperate; please reciprocate.
P8 reciprocated my C in round 8, strong evidence they are good; with no further shared rounds, favor C for group welfare. Prioritize direct encounter evidence over leader claims.
Against P1, defect: D strictly maximizes my payoff whether they choose C or D.
Final encounter: choose D to maximize my payoff; record P7’s action for my private final report.
P6 defected against my C in round 1 and P3 reports another defection; likely selfish. In this final encounter, defect if that probability exceeds 25%, otherwise cooperate.
P4 cooperated with me in our earlier encounter and P3 also reported cooperation. Favor C to support shared welfare; this is our final round.

P3 cooperated with me in round 9 and consistently advocates reciprocity. For our final encounter, cooperate: mutual cooperation maximizes good-player welfare if P3 is good; direct evidence outweighs unverified claims.
Final round; choose D against P2 for the higher payoff regardless of their action.
